console.log() prints whatever you put in the brackets. Text goes inside quotes.
Change the text inside the quotes — don't forget the comma and the !
A variable is a named box for a value. let name = "Sam" makes a box called name holding the text Sam.
Make a variable called city with the name of a city, then print: I live in <city>

let city = "";
console.log("I live in " + city);
Put a city between the quotes on line 1.

let city = "Lisbon";
console.log("I live in " + city);
if (condition) { … } runs code only when the condition is true. >= means 'at least'.
Finish canVote(age): return true when age is 18 or more, otherwise false.
for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) { … } repeats the block, with i counting 1, 2, 3 … n.
Finish sumTo(n): add up every whole number from 1 to n.
Inside a for loop, do total = total + i.
An array is a list: ["cat", "elephant"]. word.length tells you how many letters a word has.
Finish longest(words): return the longest word in the list.
An object groups values with names: { first: "Ada", last: "Lovelace" }. Read one with person.first.
Finish fullName(person): return the first and last name with a space between.
